The test image shows a tomato stem cut longitudinally at the soil line, with white material on the exterior of the stem base, dead wilted leaves, and sandy soil. This points to a soil-level stem disease.

Top candidates: Southern_Blight (white mycelial mats at stem base), Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot (white cottony mycelium on stem), Southern_Bacterial_Wilt (stem vascular discoloration). Let me view one reference per class.

Southern_Bacterial_Wilt reference (1568041) is very similar - longitudinally cut stem with brown pith discoloration. The test image (1568068) has a similar Bugwood ID. Let me check one more reference.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Stem cut longitudinally at the soil line, dead/wilted plant, roots visible in sandy soil, white material coating the stem base exterior, brown/cream internal tissue visible through the cut.

- **Southern_Blight ref**: Showed bleached/rotted stem, but no fluffy mycelial mat visible and no sclerotia matching the test.

- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot ref**: Heavy dense white cottony mycelium with dark sclerotia forming — too dense/different from test image.

- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt stem ref (1568041)**: Very similar — longitudinally cut green stem showing brown pith discoloration. Same Bugwood collection as test image (1568068). This is the diagnostic cut used to reveal vascular discoloration in bacterial wilt.

- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt root ref**: Shows brown discoloration/root rot at stem base, consistent with the dead plant and exposed roots in the test image.

The longitudinally cut stem with brown internal pith discoloration, pulled-up plant with roots, and sandy soil context all match Southern_Bacterial_Wilt. The white coating at the stem base is consistent with the "light brown discoloration in the pith area" creating a bleached appearance on exposed tissue.
